cosy-lesson.title: After Everything I've Done for You

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Transaction – An instance of buying or selling something; a business deal.

p.em: Example: Paula views her friendship with Rebecca as a debt-filled emotional transaction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Resentment – Bitter indignation at having been treated unfairly or taken for granted.

p.em: Example: Years of secret meddling build up a terrifying wave of explosive resentment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Entitlement – The amount to which a person has a right; belief that one is deserving of privileges.

p.em: Example: Her entitlement stems from believing her illegal favors buy Rebecca's total loyalty.

cosy-blockquote.p: Manipulation – The action of manipulating someone in a clever or unscrupulous way.

p.em: Example: She lists every act of manipulation as proof of her ultimate love and devotion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Obligation – An act or course of action to which a person is morally or legally bound.

p.em: Example: Creating a sense of heavy obligation is a classic guilt-trip strategy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sacrifice – An act of giving up something valued for the sake of something else.

p.em: Example: She exaggerates her personal sacrifice to make Rebecca feel completely indebted.

cosy-blockquote.p: Showstopper – A song or performance receiving prolonged applause, stopping the show.

p.em: Example: Paula delivers a jaw-dropping Gypsy-style Broadway showstopper of rage.

cosy-blockquote.p: Boundaries – A line that marks the limits of an area; emotional limits in relationships.

p.em: Example: Neither Paula nor Rebecca has any healthy respect for personal boundaries.

cosy-blockquote.p: Indebted – Owing gratitude or money to someone in return for an engine or favor.

p.em: Example: She demands that Rebecca feel forever indebted for her secret schemes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Explosive – Able or likely to shatter violently or burst out in anger.

p.em: Example: The sudden, explosive confrontation shatters their cozy dynamic.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: After everything I did for you since three years → Correct: After everything I've done for you for three years ((Use Present Perfect 'I've done' + 'for' duration.))
Incorrect: She feels indebted toward her friend → Correct: She feels indebted to her friend ((Use 'indebted to' someone.))
Incorrect: He sacrificed his career for help her → Correct: He sacrificed his career to help her ((Use 'to + infinitive' for purpose.))
